shifts.summary: The exam was overall easy to moderate with most candidates attempting 77 to 89 questions well. Reasoning was generally easy, while quantitative aptitude leaned moderate. General awareness was easy for many, and English was easy overall. Time management and the new sectional timer were common concerns.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Candidates reported many statement‑based and matrix questions, with no clock or mirror types. Reasoning was generally easy, some found it very easy.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GK mix included current affairs and static topics, candidates found it easy overall.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant was moderate overall, with many circle and trigonometry questions; time management was noted as a concern.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was easy for most candidates, with grammar and active‑passive questions common; passages were moderate in length.

asked.q: Tagore wrote a national song for Bangladesh

observations: Candidates noted time management was a challenge, especially in math and reasoning sections.
The paper pattern remained similar to previous years with no major changes.
A 15‑minute sectional timer caused difficulty for many candidates.
Overall attempts were high, with many reporting 85‑89 well‑attempted questions.
disagreements: Overall difficulty was split between Easy to Moderate (3 reports) and Moderate (3 reports).
Quant difficulty was reported as Easy by three sources and Moderate by six sources.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 7 October 2026 showed varying difficulty levels across its three shifts. Shifts 1 and 2 were reported as easy to moderate, with candidates generally attempting between 77 and 89 questions well in shift 1 and around 81 questions in shift 2. The figures presented are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts. Shift 3 analysis is pending and will be added after the shift concludes.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: According to candidate reports, shift 1 was described as easy to moderate, while shift 2 was largely reported as easy. Shift 3 has not been analysed yet, so its difficulty level will be updated later.

faqs.q: How many questions did candidates attempt well in shift 1 of the 7 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: In shift 1, candidates generally attempted between 77 and 89 questions well, according to the available reports.

faqs.q: What was the reported difficulty of the reasoning section on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: The reasoning section was reported as easy in shift 2 and generally easy in shift 1, with most candidates finding it less challenging than other sections.

faqs.q: How did candidates perform in the English section on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: English was described as easy overall in shift 1, while in shift 2 it was also easy but required more time, with most candidates attempting 21‑22 questions well.

faqs.q: When will the analysis for shift 3 of the 7 October 2026 exam be available?
faqs.a: Shift 3 analysis is pending and will be added a few hours after the shift ends, once sufficient candidate reviews are collected.
